title: Integrated Mathematics
description: Post arithmetic, integrated mathematics is an in-progress approach lightly inspired by the 1960s “new math” style of mathematics pedagogy. It begins with Basic Mathematics and works through Integrated Maths I–IV. Inspiration for course material comes from AoPS books, Apostol’s Calculus, and Harvard’s Math 55a/55b. It is a problem-solving based approach that attempts to integrate, as a treat, historical information within the course content.

title: Single Variable Calculus
description: Limits, derivatives, and integrals of single variable functions

title: Multivariable Calculus
description: Partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus

title: Studies in Algebra and Group Theory
description: Harvard Math 55a, fall 2025, taught by Denis Auroux: groups, linear algebra, bilinear forms and inner products, multilinear algebra, modules and group actions, the Sylow theorems, presentations, and the representation theory of finite groups.

title: Studies in Real and Complex Analysis
description: Real and complex analysis (Harvard Math 55 second semester)

title: Measure Theory
description: Measure and integration, following Folland’s Real Analysis; a work in progress

title: Category Theory
description: Categories, isomorphisms, opposite and product categories, and functors; in progress

title: Biology
description: Molecular biology, cell biology, genetics, and biochemistry

title: Genetic Engineering
description: MIT 9.26: genome editing, CRISPR, protein language models, spatial omics and regeneration

title: Basic Neuroscience and Geometry of Neuroscience
description: Basic Neuroscience comprises: the minimal knowledge needed to operate in the academic world and should be standard knowledge for those wishing to engage in anything orbital to neuroscience; neurons and signalling, behavior, the senses, methods and disorders, from the PSY 212 (SSU) lecture slides and my notebook. Geometry of Neuroscience is much more ambitious, though I keep them together here: Matilde Marcolli’s Caltech course on dynamical, topological, geometric and categorical models of the brain, vision and language.

title: Critical Theory
description: Frankfurt School critical theory: Lukács, Horkheimer, Adorno, Habermas, and beyond
